source.stem:
A person measures the length, width, height and mass of a metal block with rectangular sides.
Which of these measurements must be used in order to calculate the density of the metal?

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: A very tiny piece broken off a magnet is nonmagnetic and has no poles.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: The red half has only a North pole.

intelligence.enrichment: The North pole and South pole of a magnet always exist in pairs. Breaking a magnet into smaller pieces still gives pieces with both poles, so a single North pole or a single South pole cannot be obtained. dividing a magnet produces smaller magnets with paired poles rather than isolated single poles The learner explains that breaking or cutting a magnet gives smaller magnets with both North and South poles, not isolated single poles. A pole is like one end of a stick, so cutting off that end should leave one single pole.
